questions.stem: A health system shifts from fee-for-service toward value-based payment. Which statement best describes the intended change?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Payment is increasingly tied to the number of billable services delivered, while quality and patient outcomes play a smaller role in financial incentives.","B":"Payment increasingly rewards the quality and outcomes of care rather than service volume alone, aligning financial incentives with better patient care.","C":"Payment removes formal quality measurement from reimbursement decisions, allowing organizations to focus primarily on increasing procedural volume.","D":"Payment separates reimbursement from patient outcomes and care quality, because value-based models are designed only to simplify billing administration."}}
questions.rationale: CMS describes value-based programs as rewarding quality rather than service quantity alone. Option B captures that shift toward quality and outcomes. Option A describes the volume emphasis of fee-for-service rather than the intended value-based direction. Option C incorrectly removes quality measurement from reimbursement. Option D incorrectly separates payment from quality and outcomes.
questions.source_detail: CMS states that value-based programs move payment toward the quality rather than the quantity of care and link quality performance to payment; the page was modified March 10, 2026.

qc.qc_note: Strict final audit: max/min option-character ratio <=1.15; keyed option within 10% of distractor mean; keyed option is neither shortest nor longest; distractors manually reviewed for clinical plausibility, grammatical parallelism, and answer-cue leakage.
